title: Back in Class After Eight Years
script: Narrator: [nervously] On my first evening back at college, I chose a seat near the door. Everyone seemed younger, faster with the learning platform, and already familiar with academic vocabulary. I had spent eight years working in retail, and even opening the digital library felt like a test.

Narrator: The lecturer asked us to discuss an article in pairs. I understood the main idea, but my notes were a collection of disconnected sentences. My partner, Hana, had highlighted only four lines. For a moment, I assumed she was naturally better at studying.

Narrator: [curious] After class, I asked how she chose what to record. She showed me a simple system: one sentence for the author's claim, two pieces of evidence, and one question. She had learned it in a study-support workshop, not through talent.

Narrator: I attended the next workshop and brought an article from my course. The tutor did not rewrite my notes. He asked me to explain each paragraph aloud, then helped me separate examples from arguments.

Narrator: [reflective] Progress was slower than I wanted. During the first month, I needed twice as long as some classmates to prepare. But my years at work gave me strengths too: I could manage a deadline, ask practical questions, and connect theories to customer behaviour.

Narrator: I formed a small study group with Hana and another returning student. We agreed not to exchange finished answers. Instead, we compared outlines and explained confusing terms in our own words.
Narrator: [confidently] By midterm, the library no longer felt like a locked room. I still asked for help, but the questions became more precise.

Narrator: Returning to education did not require me to pretend the gap had never happened. It required a method, regular practice, and enough humility to learn skills that others had already been taught.
